title: FRAMEWORK ACT ON SETTLING THE PAST FOR TRUTH AND RECONCILIATION
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) This Act aims to contribute to national unity and the development of democracy to move toward the future by investigating anti-Japanese independence movements and cases involving violations of human rights, violence, massacres, and suspicious deaths caused by anti-democratic or anti-human rights acts, thereby establishing the truth that has been distorted or concealed and preventing recurrence, establishing the legitimacy of the nation, and promoting reconciliation with the past, including the restoration of the honor of victims and persons harmed by anti-democratic or anti-human rights acts and their surviving family members.

Article 2 (Scope of truth-finding) (1) The Truth and Reconciliation Commission under Article 4 shall establish the truth regarding the following matters:
  1. Anti-Japanese independence movements which had been carried out during the Japanese occupation or immediately prior to that period;
  2. History of overseas Koreans who have defended the sovereignty of the Republic of Korea and extended its national power after the Japanese occupation until the enforcement date of this Act (referring to the enforcement date of the Framework Act on Settling the Past for Truth and Reconciliation (Act No. 7542));
  3. Cases of collective civilian deaths, killings, injuries, disappearances, torture, or detention unlawfully committed during the period from August 15, 1945 to the period before and after the Korean War;
  4. Cases of death, injury, disappearance, torture, or detention arising from illegal or manifestly unjust exercises of public authority, such as acts undermining the constitutional order, during the period from August 15, 1945 to the time of the establishment of the National Human Rights Commission of Korea, as well as other cases of serious human rights violations and cases suspected of fabrication;
  5. Cases of terrorism, human rights abuses, violence, massacres, or suspicious deaths committed during the period from August 15, 1945 to the period of authoritarian rule by forces that deny the legitimacy of the Republic of Korea or are hostile to the Republic of Korea;
  6. Cases of human rights violations that occurred during the period from August 15, 1945 to the time of the establishment of the National Human Rights Commission of Korea in social welfare institutions, adoption agencies, and collective accommodation facilities, etc. directly operated by the State or local governments, or in social welfare institutions, adoption agencies, and collective accommodation facilities, etc. operated by private institutions supported, managed, or supervised by the State or local governments;
  7. Historically significant cases that the Truth and Reconciliation Commission under Article 4 deems truth-finding necessary for the purpose of achieving the objectives of this Act.
  (2) Even where a case falls within the scope of truth-finding under paragraph (1), cases that have received a final and conclusive judgment of a court shall be excluded; provided, an exception shall apply where the Truth and Reconciliation Commission under Article 4 determines, by resolution, that the case constitutes grounds for a retrial under the Civil Procedure Act or the Criminal Procedure Act and recognizes that truth-finding is necessary.

Article 3 (Rights of persons harmed) (1) Persons harmed and their surviving family members shall have the right to submit opinions during the truth-finding process regarding the cases referred to in the subparagraphs of Article 2(1).
  (2) The State shall guarantee the rights under paragraph (1) and shall endeavor to ensure that persons harmed and their surviving family members do not suffer further psychological distress during the truth-finding process.

Article 4 (Establishment and independence of Truth and Reconciliation Commission) (1) In order to perform the duties prescribed in this Act, a Truth and Reconciliation Commission (hereinafter referred to as the "Commission") shall be established.
  (2) The Commission shall perform the following duties:
  1. To select the subject matters of investigation and to make a decision to commence an investigation following the selection;
  2. To proceed with an investigation;
  3. Decisions on truth-finding or decisions on inability to establish the truth, based on the findigns of investigations;
  4. Exhumation of the remains of victims and memorial projects related to cases in which investigations have been commenced;
  5. Research activities for the preparation of measures for reconciliation;
  6. Matters regarding the preparation and correction of the family relations register under Article 52;
  7. Other duties that the Commission considers necessary.
  (3) The Commission shall independently perform the duties under its authority.

CHAPTER II COMPOSITION AND OPERATION OF COMMISSION

Article 5 (Organization of the Commission) (1) The Commission shall consist of 13 members, including 4 standing members.
  (2) The members shall be appointed by the President from among the following persons: 3 persons designated by the President and 10 persons elected by the National Assembly (consisting of 1 person recommended by the Speaker of the National Assembly, 4 persons recommended by the negotiating group to which the President belongs or belonged, 4 persons recommended by other negotiating groups, and 1 person recommended by a non-negotiating group):
  1. A person who has served for at least 10 years in the position of full-time professor or higher at an accredited university;
  2. A person who has served for at least 10 years in the position of judge, prosecutor, military judicial officer, or attorney-at-law;
  3. A person who has served for at least 10 years as a public official in Grade 3 or higher or as a member of the Senior Executive Service;
  4. A person who has served as a member of the clergy or has engaged for at least 10 years in research activities such as historical authentication or compilation of historical materials;
  5. Other persons deemed to have expertise and experience necessary for establishing the truth under the subparagraphs of Article 2 (1).
  (3) Of the members under paragraph (2), the standing members shall consist of 2 persons designated by the President, 1 person recommended by the negotiating group to which the President belongs or belonged, and 1 person recommended by another negotiating group.
  (4) One chairperson shall be appointed by the President from among the standing members.
  (5) The chairperson and the standing members shall serve as political appointees.

Article 6 (Term of office of the chairperson and members) (1) The term of office of the chairperson and members shall be 2 years, and they may be reappointed; provided, where the investigation period under Article 35 expires, the term of office of the members shall also expire on the date 6 months after the date of such expiration.
  (2) When the term of office of a member expires or a vacancy occurs during the term of office, a successor shall be elected or nominated within 30 days from the date when the term of office expires or the vacancy occurs, and the President shall appoint the successor immediately.
  (3) The term of office of the member who is appointed as successor of a vacancy shall start anew.

Article 7 (Composition of subcommittees) (1) The Commission may establish a subcommittee to perform part of other duties of the Commission, such as establishing the truth.
  (2) Matters necessary for the composition, duties, operation, etc. of subcommittees shall be prescribed by the rules of the Commission.

Article 8 (Duties of chairperson) (1) The chairperson shall represent the Commission and have general supervision and control of its business affairs.
  (2) When the chairperson is unable to perform his or her duties due to any unavoidable reason, a standing member designated in advance by the chairperson shall act on his or her behalf.
  (3) The chairperson may propose that the President present bills on the chairperson' duties.
  (4) In performing duties related to the budget of the Commission, the chairperson shall be deemed the head of a central government agency under Article 6 of the National Finance Act.
  (5) When the chairperson violates the Constitution or any statute in performing his or her duties, the National Assembly may adopt a resolution to institute impeachment proceedings.

Article 9 (Independence and guarantee of status of members in the performance of duties) (1) Each member shall perform his or her duties independently without any instruction or interference from others.
  (2) No member shall be dismissed from office against his or her will, except in any of the following cases:
  1. Where a physical or mental disability makes it substantially difficult for a member to perform his or her duties;
  2. Where a sentence of imprisonment without labor or heavier punishment on him or her becomes final and conclusive.
  (3) Where a member falls under paragraph (2)1, the President shall remove him or her from office upon recommendation of the chairperson following a resolution adopted on his or her removal with the concurring vote of at least 2/3 of the members.

Article 10 (Grounds for disqualification of members) (1) None of the following persons shall be qualified to be a commissioner:
  1. A person who is not a citizen of the Republic of Korea;
  2. A person falling under any subparagraph of Article 33 of the State Public Officials Act;
  3. A member of a political party;
  4. A person registered as a candidate (including a preliminary candidate) for an election to be held under the Public Official Election Act;
  5. A person removed from office under an impeachment decision.
  (2) If a member falls under any of the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), he or she shall automatically cease to hold office.

Article 11 (Prohibition of concurrent offices of members) (1) No member shall hold concurrently any office or perform duties falling under any of the following subparagraphs during his or her term of office:
  1. A member of the National Assembly or a member of a local council;
  2. A public official of another State agency or a local government (excluding educational public officials);
  3. Other positions or duties prescribed by the rules of the Commission.
  (2) No member shall join a political party or participate in political activities.

Article 12 (Exclusion, challenge, and recusal of members) (1) A member shall be excluded from deliberation and resolution where he or she falls under any of the following subparagraphs:
  1. Where the member, or his or her spouse or former spouse, is the perpetrator or person harmed in the truth-finding case by the Commission;
  2. Where the member is or was in a kinship relationship under Article 777 of the Civil Act with the perpetrator or person harmed in the truth-finding case by the Commission;
  3. Where the member was involved in an investigation or trial on the truth-finding case of the Commission;
  4. Where the member has served as a witness or expert witness regarding the truth-finding case of the Commission;
  5. Where the member has acted or has been involved as a representative of a party in relation to the truth-finding case of the Commission.
  (2) An applicant for truth-finding under Article 22 or a person subject to investigation under Article 26 may file a motion to challenge a member with the Commission where it is impracticable to expect fairness in the deliberation and resolution by the member.
  (3) If a member considers that he or she falls under any of the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) or the grounds under paragraph (2), he or she may voluntarily recuse himself or herself from deliberation and resolution.

Article 13 (Proceedings and quorum of meetings) Meetings of the Commission and its subcommittees shall be presided over by the respective chairperson, and unless otherwise provided in this Act, resolutions shall be adopted by an affirmative vote of a majority of the incumbent members.

Article 14 (Disclosure of proceedings) (1) Proceedings of the Commission shall be open to the public; provided, they may be closed if the Commission or a subcommittee deems it necessary.
  (2) Disclosure under paragraph (1) shall be made by such methods as disclosure of minutes, public attendance at meetings, or broadcasting or Internet transmission.
  (3) Even where it is decided not to disclose the proceedings under the proviso of paragraph (1), the minutes including the grounds for nondisclosure and other matters prescribed by the rules of the Commission shall be disclosed.

Article 15 (Meeting minutes) (1) The Commission shall prepare and preserve minutes recording the date and time and place of meetings, attendees, agenda items, details of deliberations, and matters resolved.
  (2) The minutes shall be disclosed; provided, when the chairperson deems it necessary for the protection of the public interest or for other reasons, all or part thereof may remain undisclosed by resolution of the Commission.
  (3) Matters necessary for the scope, method, and procedure for preparing, preserving, and disclosing the meeting minutes under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by the rules of the Commission.

Article 16 (Establishment of Secretariat) (1) A Secretariat shall be established within the Commission to handle the business affairs of the Commission.
  (2) The Secretariat shall have 1 secretary-general and other staff members, and the secretary-general shall be appointed by the President upon the recommendation of the chairperson following deliberation by the Commission.
  (3) Among staff members of the Secretariat, public officials of Grade III or higher shall be appointed by the President on the recommendation of the chairperson, and public officials of Grade IV or lower shall be appointed by the chairperson on the recommendation of the secretary-general.
  (4) The secretary-general shall take charge of the administrative affairs of the Secretariat and give directions to and supervise staff members of the Secretariat, under the direction of the chairperson.
  (5) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Secretariat shall be prescribed by the rules of the Commission.

Article 17 (Establishment of advisory bodies) (1) The Commission may establish advisory bodies in order to obtain advice on matters necessary for the performance of its duties.
  (2) Members of the advisory bodies established under paragraph (1) shall be commissioned by the chairperson following a resolution by the Commission, from among historical researchers, forensic experts, leaders in society and religion, public officials with professional knowledge and experience, and persons representing relevant private organizations.
  (3) The Commission may establish advisory bodies for each subcommittee.
  (4) Matters necessary for the composition, operation, and commissioning, etc. of the advisory bodies shall be prescribed by the rules of the Commission.

Article 18 (Collection of opinions of persons harmed) (1) In order to enhance public consensus and agreement in performing its duties, the Commission shall establish a forum for collecting opinions (hereinafter referred to as the "Deliberative Public Forum") on matters including the composition and operation of the Commission, the truth-finding process, the protection of the rights of persons harmed, compensation and reparation for damages, and restoration of honor.
  (2) The Commission shall ensure fair opportunities for participation and procedures for collecting opinions in the composition and operation of the Deliberative Public Forum.
  (3) Participants in the Deliberative Public Forum shall be composed of persons recommended in equal numbers by organizations of persons harmed related to truth-finding and by standing members.
  (4) Matters regarding the method of composition and operation of the Deliberative Public Forum and other related matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 19 (Guarantee of status of staff members) (1) No Commission staff member shall be forced to retire, placed on leave, demoted, or dismissed against his or her will, except upon a final criminal judgment or disciplinary action.
  (2) Commission staff members, with the exception of dispatched public officials, shall have the authority and responsibilities as public officials in special service under the State Public Officials Act for the operating period of the Commission.

Article 20 (Establishment of disciplinary committee) (1) A disciplinary committee shall be established in the Commission to resolve any disciplinary action against staff members of the Commission.
  (2) The composition, authority, and deliberation procedures of the disciplinary committee, types and effects of disciplinary actions, and other necessary matters therefor shall be prescribed by the rules of the Commission.

Article 21 (Composition and operation of Commission) Except as provided in this Act, matters necessary for the composition, operation, etc. of the Commission shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER III DUTIES AND AUTHORITY OF COMMISSION

Article 22 (Application for truth-finding) (1) A victim, a person harmed, or a surviving family member thereof, a person in a familial relationship, or a person having special knowledge of facts regarding a truth-finding case of the Commission may file an application for truth-finding with the Commission.
  (2) An application under paragraph (1) shall be filed within 2 years from the date this Act enters into force; provided, even after the expiration of such period, an additional application period may be prescribed by resolution of the Commission.
  (3) The scope of persons related by kinship under paragraph (1) and persons having special knowledge of facts shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 23 (Form of application) (1) An application under Article 22 shall be made in writing stating the matters in the following subparagraphs; provided, if special circumstances exist making it impracticable to submit a written application, it may be made orally:
  1. The name and address of the applicant;
  2. The purpose of the application for truth-finding and the fact that constitutes the cause thereof.
  (2) Matters necessary for procedures, methods, etc. for filing an application under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 24 (Decision of dismissal without prejudice) (1) Where an application for truth-finding falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Commission shall dismiss the application without prejudice and without conducting an investigation:
  1. Where an application for truth-finding does not fall under any subject matter of investigation for ascertaining the truth by the Commission;
  2. Where the content itself of the application for truth-finding is deemed obviously false or groundless;
  3. Where the application for clarifying the truth is filed again on the same facts with regard to which an earlier application was dismissed without prejudice by the Commission; provided, this shall not apply where the applicant submits important explanatory materials not submitted earlier.
  (2) Where an application for clarifying the truth falls under any of the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), the Commission shall dismiss the application without prejudice even after it has decided to initiate an investigation.

Article 25 (Commencement of truth-finding investigations) (1) If an application for truth-finding does not fall under any of the grounds prescribed in the subparagraphs of Article 24(1), the Commission shall commence an investigation without delay and conduct such investigation as necessary concerning the matters stated therein.
  (2) If necessary prior to the commencement of an investigation, the Commission may conduct a preliminary investigation to determine whether to commence the investigation.
  (3) The Commission may investigate ex officio where it determines that truth-finding is necessary with respect to a case that is historically significant or constitutes a serious human rights violation. In such cases, the scope of the ex officio investigation shall be determined by a resolution of the Commission.
  (4) Where a serious human rights violation is discovered in the course of an investigation, even though no application for truth-finding has been filed with respect thereto, the Commission shall investigate ex officio and establish the truth of the case.

Article 26 (Methods of truth-finding investigation) (1) In conducting an investigation, the Commission may take any of the following measures:
  1. Requesting a person subject to investigation and a person for reference to submit a written statement;
  2. Requesting a person subject to investigation and a person for reference to appear before the Commission, and hearing their statements;
  3. Requesting a person subject to investigation, an expert witness, and other relevant agencies, facilities, organizations, etc. to submit relevant materials or articles, and keeping in custody submitted materials;
  4. Inquiring of relevant agencies, facilities, organizations, etc. about facts or information deemed related to the investigation;
  5. Designating an expert witness and requesting him or her to conduct appraisal.
  (2) When the Commission deems it necessary, it may have a commissioner or staff member of the Commission take any measure falling under any of the subparagraphs of paragraph (1).
  (3) Where necessary for taking any measure under any of the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), the Commission may request relevant agencies, including the Ministry of the Interior and Safety and the Supreme Court, to submit materials concerning personal information, such as resident registration data and family relation registration data. In such cases, the relevant agencies that receive such request shall submit the requested materials.
  (4) The Commission may, by resolution, have a member or a staff member of the Commission conduct an on-site investigation of relevant materials or objects, or of institutions, facilities, or organizations (hereinafter referred to as "agencies, etc."), at the place where the facts that caused the truth-finding case occurred or at any other necessary place. In such cases, the member or staff member shall carry identification verifying his or her authority and present it to the relevant persons.
  (5) If a member or a staff member of the Commission hears statements under subparagraph 2 of paragraph (1), Articles 147 through 149 and 244-3 of the Criminal Procedure Act shall apply mutatis mutandis.
  (6) A member or a staff member of the Commission who conducts an on-site investigation under paragraph (4) may request agencies, etc. subject to the investigation to submit necessary materials or objects, and the agencies, etc. that receive such a request shall comply therewith unless there exist special circumstances.
  (7) With respect to a request for the submission of necessary materials or objects under subparagraph 3 of paragraph (1) or (6), Articles 110 through 112, 129 through 131, and 133 of the Criminal Procedure Act shall apply mutatis mutandis;provided that agencies, etc. refusing to submit such materials or objects shall specifically explain the grounds therefor.
  (8) Where the Commission determines that the explanation under paragraph (7) is unfounded after reviewing it, the Commission may, by resolution, order the submission of the materials or tangible things.
  (9) Institutions, etc. that receive an order from the Commission to submit materials or objects in relation to an on-site investigation or truth-finding shall not refuse such submission on the grounds of the National Intelligence Service Act, the Act on the Employees of the National Intelligence Service, the Military Secret Protection Act, the Protection of Military Bases and Installations Act, or any other such statute, and where the materials or objects do not exist, they shall notify the Commission of that fact;provided that the materials or objects need not be submitted where the competent Minister (or, in the case of an institution affiliated with the President or the Prime Minister, the head of the relevant institution) submits, within 5 days from the date on which the order for submission was received, an explanation that the matters constitute State secrets relating to military, diplomatic, or inter-Korean relations and that disclosure thereof would have a significant impact on national security.
  (10) Notwithstanding the proviso to paragraph (9), the head of an agency, etc. that receives an order for the submission of materials or tangible things shall take measures to allow the Commission to inspect only the relevant materials or tangible things; provided, the Commission that has inspected such materials or tangible things shall not disclose them.

Article 27 (Exhumation of remains and compensation for loss) (1) For the purpose of truth-finding, the Commission shall establish a unit dedicated to the exhumation of remains to perform duties relating to the investigation, exhumation, and identification of the remains of victims (hereinafter referred to as the "remains of victims") in connection with cases for which an investigation has been commenced under Article 25.
  (2) Where there are reasonable grounds to believe that the remains of victims are buried in land, public waters, or other such places (hereinafter referred to as "land, etc."), the Commission may investigate and recover such remains and may enter upon or temporarily use the land, etc. of another person to the extent necessary for such investigation and exhumation, and may remove or alter obstacles such as crops or trees, if unavoidable.
  (3) When the Commission intends to investigate or recover the remains of victims, it shall prepare an investigation and exhumation plan in advance and notify the owner, possessor, or manager of the relevant land, etc., as well as other interested persons.
  (4) No person shall damage or arbitrarily dispose of the remains of victims or their personal effects.
  (5) The State shall preserve exhumed remains as prescribed by Presidential Decree and may carry out memorial projects.
  (6) When there are reasonable grounds to recognize that exhumed remains are those of victims, the Commission may take measures necessary for identification, including the collection of DNA samples, and if necessary, may conduct genetic testing of the exhumed remains and their family members as prescribed by the Bioethics and Safety Act.
  (7) If the Commission causes loss to another person due to entry upon or temporary use of land, etc., or the removal or alteration of obstacles such as crops or trees in the course of investigation and exhumation under paragraph (2), it shall provide compensation therefor. In such cases, the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, etc. for Public Works Projects shall apply mutatis mutandis to the standards for compensation for loss.
  (8) Matters necessary for the establishment and operation of the unit dedicated to the exhumation of remains under paragraph (1), the investigation and exhumation of remains under paragraph (2), and the procedures for compensation for loss under paragraph (7) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 28 (Order to accompany) (1) Of persons who have been requested to appear under Article 26(1)2, if a person, who possesses decisive evidentiary materials or information regarding the truth distorted or concealed by the exercise of public authority that is anti-democratic or violates human rights, fails to comply with such request for appearance on 3 or more occasions without good cause, the Commission may, by resolution, issue a warrant of accompaniment ordering that person to accompany.
  (2) A warrant of accompaniment under paragraph (1) shall state the name and residence of the person subject thereto, the grounds for the order to accompany, the place to which the person shall be brought, the date of issuance, the period of validity of the warrant, a statement to th effect that the warrant shall not be executed after the expiration of such period and shall be returned, and a statement to the effect that an administrative fine shall be imposed where the person refuses to comply with the order to accompany, and the warrant shall be signed and sealed by the Chairperson. When the name of the person subject thereto is uncertain, the person may be identified by description of appearance, physique, or other identifying characteristics; and where the residence is uncertain, the statement of residence may be omitted.
  (3) A warrant of accompanying shall be served by presenting it to the relevant person.
  (4) The execution of the order to accompany is carried out by the staff of the committee.
  (5) A warrant of accompanying to an inmate in a correctional facility or detention center (including a military correctional facility or military detention center) shall be served by a correctional officer through delegation by a staff member of the Commission.
  (6) Where the relevant person is an active-duty soldier in a military camp, the commander of the unit to which the person belongs shall be obligated to cooperate with a staff member of the Commission in the service of the warrant of accompanying on such person.

Article 29 (Conduct of Hearings) (1) The Commission may hold hearings by its resolution to hear testimony, appraisal, and statements from witnesses, appraisers, and expert witnesses and to adopt evidence, where deemed necessary to perform its duties.
  (2) The Commission shall not hold any hearing for the purpose of infringing the privacy of an individual or intervening in an ongoing court proceeding or the prosecution of a case under investigation.
  (3) The hearing shall not be open to the public. However, it may be made public by resolution of the committee.
  (4) Procedures and methods for holding hearings by the Commission pursuant to paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by the rules of the Commission.

Article 30 (Request for attendance of witnesses) (1) Where the Commission requests the submission of materials or objects or the attendance of witnesses, appraisers, and expert witnesses in relation to hearings, the chairperson shall issue a written request to the relevant persons or the heads of the relevant agencies.
  (2) Where the Commission requests the submission of materials under paragraph (1), the chairperson may require the materials to be submitted in writing, electronically, or as recorded on the magnetic tape or magnetic disk of a computer or other similar media, or to be entered in a computer network.
  (3) A written request issued pursuant to paragraph (1) shall state the date, time, and place on and at which materials or objects shall be submitted or a witness, appraiser, or expert witness shall attend, and the legal sanctions to be imposed for failure to comply with the request of the Commission, and a written request issued to a witness or an expert witness shall additionally state substantial issues to be examined.
  (4) A written request issued under paragraph (1) shall be served seven days prior to the date by which the materials or objects shall be submitted or the date a witness, expert witness, or person to be questioned shall attend.
  (5) The provisions of the Civil Procedure Act regarding the service of documents shall apply mutatis mutandis to the service of written requests under paragraph (1).
  (6) A witness or an expert witness requested to attend may submit beforehand a written answer to the substantial issues to be examined.
  (7) Paragraphs (7) through (10) of Article 26 shall apply mutatis mutandis to a request for submission of materials or articles under paragraph (1).

Article 31 (Duty of witnesses to appear) (1) Any person requested by the Commission to submit materials or articles, or to appear as a witness or an appraiser under Article 30(1), shall comply therewith, notwithstanding other statutes.
  (2) Article 3 of the Act on Testimony and Appraisal before the National Assembly shall apply mutatis mutandis to a person requested by the Commission to appear as a witness or an appraiser under Article 30(1).
  (3) If a public official or a person who was a public official is requested to testify, Article 26(9) shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 32 (Oaths of witnesses) (1) Where the chairperson requires a witness to testify at a hearing or an appraiser to provide an appraisal at a hearing, the witness or appraiser shall be required to take an oath.
  (2) Where a person who attends a hearing as a person to be questioned consents to take an oath as a witness, such person may be examined as a witness.
  (3) The chairperson shall fully explain the meaning of an oath and inform that a punishment shall be imposed for perjury or a false expert opinion before a witness or expert witness takes an oath.
  (4) Article 157 of the Criminal Procedure Act shall apply mutatis mutandis where a person takes an oath as a witness under paragraphs (1) and (2).
  (5) Article 170 of the Criminal Procedure Act shall apply mutatis mutandis where an expert witness takes an oath pursuant to paragraph (1).

Article 33 (Protection of witnesses) (1) A witness may be accompanied by counsel, who is an attorney-at-law, to a hearing to seek advice on his or her legal rights. In such cases, the counsel shall submit a document certifying his or her qualification as an attorney-at-law.
  (2) No witness, expert witness, or reference witness shall be subject to any disadvantageous disposition, other than punishment prescribed by this Act, on account of any testimony, expert opinion, or statement given at a hearing.

Article 34 (Verification) (1) Where necessary for hearings, the Commission may verify materials or objects deemed related to the case subject to investigation, by its resolution.
  (2) Where the Commission verifies materials or articles pursuant to paragraph (1), the chairperson shall issue a notice of conducting verification to a manager of the materials or articles subject to verification (in cases of a State agency, etc., referring to the head of the State agency). In such cases, the notice of conducting verification shall be delivered three days prior to the date of verification.
  (3) A notice of conducting verification given under paragraph (2) shall state members who conduct verification, the purpose, subject matters, and methods of verification, the date, time, and place of verification, and other matters necessary for verification.
  (4) Article 26 (9) shall apply mutatis mutandis to verification under paragraph (1).
  (5) The provisions of the Civil Procedure regarding the service of documents shall apply mutatis mutandis to the service of a notice of conducting verification under paragraph (2).

Article 35 (Period of investigation) (1) The Commission shall conduct activities to ascertain the truth for 3 years from the date the first determination on initiation of the investigation for ascertaining the truth is made, after its composition.
  (2) If it is impracticable to complete the truth-finding activities within the investigation period referred to in paragraph (1), the Commission may extend the period, on not more than two occasions, by up to one year each time after reporting to the President and the National Assembly three months before the period expires.
  (3) If the Commission determines that there is no need to continue the investigation before the expiration of the investigation period under paragraphs (1) and (2), it may terminate the investigation by resolution of the Commission.

Article 36 (Decision on truth-finding) Where an investigation is concluded and the truth is verified, the Commission shall determine the results of the investigation by resolution.

Article 37 (Decision on inability to establish the truth) Where the Commission fails to establish the truth or is unable to do so based on the findings of the investigation, it shall make a decision of inability to establish the truth, stating the reasons therefor.

Article 38 (Notice of decisions and objections) (1) Where the Commission renders a decision of dismissal under Article 24, a decision to commence an investigation under Article 25, a decision on truth-finding under Article 36, or a decision on inability to verify the truth under Article 37, it shall, without delay, notify the applicant for truth-finding under Article 22 and the person subject to investigation and witnesses under Article 26 thereof, specifying the grounds therefor.
  (2) Where the applicant for truth-finding under Article 22 or the person subject to investigation under Article 26 has died or his or her whereabouts are unknown, notice shall be given to his or her spouse or lineal ascendants or descendants.
  (3) In giving notice under paragraphs (1) and (2), the Commission shall inform the person notified of the filing of an objection, procedures and period for filing an objection, and other necessary matters.
  (4) Where a person in receipt of notice under paragraphs (1) and (2) is dissatisfied with the contents of notice, he or she may file an objection with the Commission in writing within 60 days after the receipt thereof.
  (5) The Commission shall make a decision on any objection filed, within 60 days from the date of receipt thereof, and shall notify the results thereof to the person who has filed the objection, in writing without delay.
  (6) Matters regarding the procedures for filing an objection under paragraph (4) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 39 (Disclosure of decisions) The Commission shall disclose the contents of a decision of dismissal under Article 24, a decision of truth-finding under Article 36, and a decision of inability to ascertain the truth under Article 37; provided, if it is necessary for national security or national reconciliation, the Commission need not disclose such contents by resolution, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 40 (Dispatch of public officials) (1) If the chairperson deems it necessary for the performance of the Commission's duties, the chairperson may request the head of a State agency or local government to dispatch public officials under their jurisdiction to serve at the Commission and to provide the support necessary therefor. In such cases, the head of the state agency or local government who has received such request for dispatch shall cooperate promptly unless they demonstrate that such cooperation would cause a significant impediment to the performance of duties.
  (2) Public officials dispatched to the Commission under paragraph (1) shall perform the duties of the Commission independently from their affiliated State agency or local government.
  (3) The head of the State agency or local government that has dispatched public officials under paragraph (1) shall not take any adverse personnel action against a person dispatched to the Commission.
  (4) If the Commission determines that a dispatched public official performs the duties of the Commission in an insincere manner or is otherwise unsuitable for performing such duties, the Commission may request the head of the relevant state agency or local government to replace such person, and the head of the state agency or local government shall cooperate promptly and actively with such request.

Article 41 (Protection of members) (1) No person shall assault or intimidate a member, an employee, or a member of an advisory body engaged in the performance of official duties, or obstruct the performance of such duties by deceit.
  (2) No person shall assault or threaten a member, an employee, or a member of an advisory body for the purpose of compelling or preventing any act in connection with his or her duties, or causing him or her to resign from office.
  (3) No person shall obstruct, by assault, intimidation, or deceit, the appearance, testimony, expert opinion, or statement of a witness, an expert witness, or a reference witness, or the submission of materials or objects.
  (4) No person shall suffer any disadvantage, such as dismissal, suspension, pay reduction, or transfer, on the ground that they have provided or intend to provide information in connection with the investigation of a truth-finding case.
  (5) The Commission shall take measures necessary to protect reference witnesses, witnesses, or expert witnesses in a truth-finding case, and to secure related materials or prevent the destruction thereof.
  (6) The Commission may provide necessary rewards or support to a person who has revealed the truth of a truth-finding case or discovered or submitted materials important for truth-finding, and may recommend such person as a candidate for pardon. The details and procedures for such rewards or support, and other necessary matters, shall be prescribed by the rules of the Commission.

Article 42 (Protection of persons subject to investigation) (1) No person shall disclose that a person committed a perpetrating act related to any case falling under any subparagraph of Article 2(1) solely on the ground that such person held a specific position in an administrative agency, the military, the judiciary, an organization, or a group during the period subject to the scope of truth-finding under the subparagraphs of Article 2(1).
  (2) In the course of an investigation, the Commission shall exercise care not to infringe upon the privacy and reputation of a person subject to investigation, and shall prepare measures to protect the privacy and reputation of such person.

Article 43 (Reporting and opportunity to state opinions) (1) The Commission shall prepare an investigation report on its activities and report thereon to the President and the National Assembly twice each year.
  (2) Upon completion of the activities of the Commission, the Commission shall prepare a comprehensive report covering the entire activities of the Commission and report thereon to the President and the National Assembly within 6 months.
  (3) When investigating the conduct of a person subject to investigation, the Commission shall grant the person subject to investigation under Article 26, his or her spouse, lineal descendants, or interested persons an opportunity to state their opinions. In such cases, a person who is to state their opinions may request an inspection of the evidentiary materials forming the basis for the preparation of the investigation report, and may appoint legal counsel.
  (4) The investigation report under paragraph (1) and the comprehensive report under paragraph (2) shall include recommendations on the following matters:
  1. Measures to be taken by the State to restore the damage suffered by victims and persons harmed and to restore their reputation;
  2. Measures to be taken by the State to prevent the recurrence of truth-finding cases and to recover the damage suffered by victims and persons harmed.
  3. Measures that the State must take to prevent recurrence of cases subject to ascertaining the truth;
  4. Matters regarding rectifying, amending, and repealing relevant statutes and regulations, systems, policies, and practices;
  5. Matters regarding legal and political reconciliation measures for perpetrators in truth-finding cases;
  6. Measures to be taken by the State to promote national reconciliation and development of democracy;
  7. Measures to be taken by the State regarding education and publicity to raise historical awareness;
  8. Other matters that the Commission deems necessary to accomplish the purpose of this Act.
  (5) If the Commission has reported to the President and the National Assembly under paragraphs (1) and (2), it shall disclose the relevant report without delay;provided, if the Commission determines that it is unavoidable not to disclose a part of the report for the purposes of national security, national reconciliation, or democratic development, it need not disclose a part of the report.

Article 44 (Duty of State agencies to endeavor to implement recommendations) (1) A State agency having jurisdiction over the recommendations under Article 43(4) (hereinafter referred to as the "competent State agency") shall respect such recommendations and endeavor to implement them.
  (2) The Prime Minister shall monitor and manage the status of implementation of the recommendations by the competent State agencies under paragraph (1).
  (3) The head of a competent State agency shall submit to the Prime Minister an implementation plan for the recommendations under its jurisdiction included in the report within 3 months from the date on which the Commission reported under Article 43(1) or (2), and shall submit the results of measures taken when such recommendations have been implemented.
  (4) If the head of a competent State agency fails to implement all or a part of the recommendations, such head shall submit to the Prime Minister a written statement of the reasons therefor.
  (5) Except as provided in paragraphs (2) through (4), matters necessary for the submission, monitoring, etc. of the compliance plans, the results of measures taken, and causes for non-compliance shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 45 (Duty of cooperation of State agencies) (1) Relevant agencies, such as the State agencies and local governments, shall be obliged to provide proactive cooperation and convenience necessary for ascertaining the truth for the performance of the Commission's duties.
  (2) When the Commission deems it necessary for the performance of its duties, it may perform such duties with the assistance of relevant agencies, including local governments.
  (3) A State agency may establish a special body separate from the Commission for truth-finding.

Article 46 (Request for application for warrant of seizure or search) (1) If an individual, agency, or other entity possessing materials or articles necessary for truth-finding refuses to submit them without good cause despite the Commission's request, the Commission may request the chief prosecutor of the competent district prosecutors' office to apply for a warrant for search, seizure, or inspection.
  (2) When requesting a warrant application, the Commission shall specify the specific scope necessary for the investigation and attach materials substantiating the necessity of such request, such as interview records of a person subject to investigation and investigation reports.
  (3) Where a prosecutor of the competent District Prosecutors' Office receives a request under paragraph (1) and deems the Commission's request necessary for the investigation, he or she shall promptly apply for a warrant to a judge of the competent court; where he or she decides not to file such application, he or she shall immediately notify the Commission in writing of the reasons therefor.
  (4) The Commission may apply to a prosecutor for inspection or copying of materials submitted under paragraph (1) to the extent necessary for the investigation, and the prosecutor shall comply with the Commission's request unless there is a special reason not to do so.

Article 47 (Accusation and request for investigation) (1) When the Commission confirms that the contents of truth-finding are factual and deems that there is suspicion of a crime, it may file an accusation with the head of an investigative agency; provided, if the person suspected of the crime is a military officer or a military civilian employee, it may file the accusation with the Chief of Staff of the relevant armed service or the Minister of National Defense.
  (2) If the Commission recognizes a substantial probability of a suspected crime according to a truth-finding investigation, it may request the competent investigative agency to conduct an investigation.
  (3) The Minister of National Defense, the Chief of Staff of the respective military branch, or the head of an investigative agency receiving a criminal complaint or a request for investigation under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall take necessary measures without delay and notify the Commission of the results.
  (4) Upon receiving the notification under paragraph (3), the Commission shall notify the applicant for truth-finding under Article 22 in writing of the gist thereof without delay.

CHAPTER IV MEASURES BY THE STATE AND COMMISSION FOR RECONCILIATION

Article 48 (Responsibilities of the State and local governments) (1) The State shall take measures necessary for the recovery from damage, restoration of reputation, prevention of recurrence, and national reconciliation and integration, including compensation or indemnification for damage suffered by victims of truth-finding cases.
  (2) Local governments shall establish and implement policy measures necessary for the recovery from damage and restoration of reputation of victims of truth-finding cases.

Article 49 (Prohibition of disadvantage) No person shall inflict any disadvantage upon another person on the ground of facts ascertained pursuant to this Act except in accordance with lawful procedures.

Article 50 (Restitution or compensation for damage and restoration of honor) (1) The State shall prepare measures for compensation or indemnification for damage suffered by victims, persons harmed, and surviving family members and for the restoration of their reputation in accordance with the truth ascertained.
  (2) The standards, scope, types, and the like of restitution or compensation under paragraph (1) shall be separately prescribed by statutes.
  (3) If measures under paragraph (1) or (2) are being implemented under other statutes, paragraph (1) or (2) shall not apply.

Article 51 (Recommendation of special pardon and restoration of rights for victims) The Commission may recommend to the President a special pardon and restoration of rights for persons who were convicted due to the concealment or distortion of the truth, or whose qualifications were lost or suspended under statutes and regulations, and relevant State agencies shall respect the decisions and recommendations of the Commission.

Article 52 (Creation and correction of family relations registers) If a family relations register for a person harmed was not created at the time of the case subject to a truth-finding decision, or if it was recorded incorrectly, the family relations register may be created or its records may be corrected under the procedures prescribed by Supreme Court Regulations if the Commission so decides, notwithstanding other statutes and regulations.

Article 53 (Reconciliation measures for perpetrators confessing the complete truth) (1) If a perpetrator actively cooperates in truth-finding by voluntarily admitting the perpetrating act during the course of truth-finding and the admitted contents conform to the truth, the Commission may recommend to the relevant agencies that the perpetrator not be punished or that the punishment be mitigated in investigative and trial proceedings, and where the perpetrator has been found guilty in accordance with criminal procedure, the Commission may recommend to the President special pardon and retoration of rights as prescribed by statutes.
  (2) Relevant agencies shall respect the decisions and recommendations of the Commission.

Article 54 (Reconciliation between perpetrators and persons harmed and surviving family members) The Commission and the Government shall actively strive for reconciliation between perpetrators and persons harmed and surviving family members to ensure the repentance of perpetrators and the forgiveness of persons harmed and surviving family members.

Article 55 (Establishment of Foundation on the Research of the Past) (1) The Government may contribute funds to establish the Foundation on the Research of the Past which will conduct memorial projects and establish, operate, and manage archives.
  (2) Paragraph (1) shall not preclude the contribution of funds in other forms.
  (3) The Past Affairs Research Foundation shall be in charge of the following projects:
  1. Memorial projects and the establishment, operation, and management of the archives;
  2. Support for further truth-seeking projects;
  3. Support for cultural and academic activities related to truth-finding.
  4. Other necessary matters.
  (4) The independence of the Past Affairs Research Foundation shall be guaranteed.

Article 56 (Promotion of commemoration and memorial projects) (1) The State and local governments may designate a commemorative day or a memorial day in order to remember cases for which a truth-finding decision has been made and to commemorate the victims and persons harmed thereof, and may hold various events to honor persons related to such cases.
  (2) The State and local governments may jointly promote or entrust the implementation of commemorative and memorial projects under paragraph (1) to public institutions or private organizations, and in such cases may provide support within the budget.

CHAPTER V SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 57 (Duty of Confidentiality) No person who is or was a member of the Commission, a staff member of the Commission, a member of an advisory body or a deliberative public forum, an appraiser, or an expert or a private organization and its personnel who participated in investigations or performed duties for the Commission upon the Commission's request shall provide or divulge to any other person information, documents, materials, or objects classified as confidential by the Commission, or use them for any purpose other than the performance of the Commission's duties.

Article 58 (Prohibition of impersonation of qualifications) No person shall exercise the authority of the Commission by impersonating a member of the Commission, a staff member thereof, or a member of an advisory body, or by falsely claiming that he or she has been delegated, entrusted, or jointly assigned to perform the duties of the Commission.

Article 59 (Prohibition on use of similar name) No person, other than the Commission, shall use the name "Truth and Reconciliation Commission" or any similar name.

Article 60 (Restriction on organization of groups supporting persons harmed) No person shall form an organization for the purpose of making profits under the pretext of supporting persons harmed or their surviving family members, or conduct a collective or individual action.

Article 61 (Special cases concerning the statute of limitations for claims for damages) With respect to claims for damages arising from harm caused by a case for which a truth-finding decision has been made, Articles 166(1) and 766(2) of the Civil Act and Article 96(2) of the National Finance Act shall not apply.

CHAPTER VI PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 62 (Legal fiction as public officials for purposes of applying penalty provisions) Any member of the Commission who is not a public official shall be deemed a public official for purposes of applying penalty provisions under the Criminal Act or other statutes.

Article 63 (Penalty provisions) (1) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment with prison labor for not more than 5 years or by a fine not exceeding 60 million won:
  1. A person who interferes with the performance of the duties of a commissioner or staff member of the Commission or a member of an advisory organization by violence, threat, or deception, in violation of Article 41 (1);
  2. A person who commits violence or intimidation against a commissioner or staff member of the Commission or a member of an advisory organization, with intent to compel him or her to do any act in the course of performing the duties, to deter him or her from doing it, or to resign him or her from the post, in violation of Article 41 (2);
  3. A witness who provides false testimony or an appraiser who makes a false appraisal after taking an oath at a hearing.
  (2) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for up to 3 years or by a fine not exceeding 30 million won:
  1. A person who files a false application for truth-finding under Article 22, with the intention of defaming another person or with knowledge that such act constitutes hindrance to the Commission in performing its duties;
  2. A person who defames another person alive or deceased by disclosure, in violation of Article 42(1);
  3. A person who fails to comply with an order to submit materials or articles related to a hearing without good cause;
  4. A witness who refuses to attend a hearing, take an oath, or present testimony at the hearing without good cause;
  5. An expert witness who refuses to take an oath or to conduct an appraisal at a hearing without good cause;
  6. A person who interferes with the attendance of a witness, expert witness, or person to be questioned at a hearing or verification without good cause.
  (3) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than 2 years or by a fine not exceeding 20 million won:
  1. A person who provides or divulges any confidential information, etc. in violation of Article 57 or uses it for any other purpose than performing the duties of the Commission;
  2. A person who exercises the authority of the Commission by falsely pretending to be a member, etc. of the Commission, by falsely pretending to have been delegated or entrusted with the duties of the Commission, or by falsely pretending to jointly perform the duties of the Commission, in violation of Article 58.
  3. 3. A person who organizes a group or engages in group or individual activities for the purpose of profit, in violation of Article 60.
  (4) A person who violates Article 27(4) by damaging or arbitrarily disposing of the remains or personal effects of a victim shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than 1 year or by a fine not exceeding 10 million won.

Article 64 (Joint penalty provisions) If a representative of a corporation or an organization, or an agent, employee, or other servant of a corporation, an organization, or an individual commits an act in violation of Article 63 in connection with the business of such corporation, organization, or individual, not only shall the actor be punished, but the corporation, organization, or individual shall also be punished by the fine prescribed in the relevant Article; provided, this shall not apply where such corporation, organization, or individual has not been negligent in giving due care and supervision concerning the relevant business to prevent such violation.

Article 65 (Mitigation of punishment) (1) If a witness or an appraiser who has taken an oath under this Act gives false testimony or an expert opinion but confesses such act before the crime is discovered, the punishment may be reduced or exempted.
  (2) The confession referred to in paragraph (1) shall be made before the Commission makes a final decision on the relevant case subject to ascertaining the truth.

Article 66 (Administrative fines) (1) Any of the following persons shall be punished by an administrative fine not exceeding 30 million won:
  1. An expert witness who makes a false statement (including the submission of a written statement) or a person who submits false materials or objects requested by the Commission for the purposes of interfering with activities to establish the truth of the Commission;
  2. A person who falsely replies to the inquiries made under Article 26(1)4;
  3. A person who fails to comply with an order to submit materials or articles under Article 26(8) without good cause.
  (2) Any of the following persons shall be punished by an administrative fine not exceeding 10 million won:
  1. A person who refuses, evades, or obstructs an on-site investigation under Article 26 (4) without good cause;
  2. A person who fails to comply with an order to accompany prescribed in Article 28 without good cause;
  3. A person who disadvantages a person who provided or intends to provide information regarding an investigation of a truth-finding case, in violation of Article 41(4);
  4. A person who gives a disadvantage to other persons, in violation of Article 49;
  5. A person who uses the name "Truth and Reconciliation Commission" or any name similar thereto, in violation of Article 59.
  (3) Administrative fines under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be imposed by the Chairperson as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

ADDENDA <Act No. 21330, Feb. 5, 2026>
Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Act shall enter into force on February 26, 2026; provided, the amended provisions of Articles 18, 27, 39, 44, and 63(4) shall enter into force 6 months after the date of its promulgation.
Article 2 (Preparatory acts for enforcement of this Act)
Preparations for the composition of the Commission, such as the appointment of its commissioners and staff members who conduct truth-finding activities according to the enforcement of this Act and for the establishment of necessary organizations including the secretariat, the enactment of and amendment to the rules of the Commission necessary for the enforcement of this Act, and other preparatory acts for the enforcement of this Act may be performed before this Act enters into force.
Article 3 (Applicability to commencement of terms of office of commissioners)
The term of office of the members appointed under this Act shall be deemed to begin on the date this Act enters into force.
Article 4 (Applicability to creation and correction of family relations registers)
The amended provisions of Article 52 shall also apply to persons harmed in cases where the former Commission made a truth-finding decision under the previous provisions.
Article 5 (Applicability to special cases concerning the statute of limitations for claims for damages)
The amended provisions of Article 61 shall also apply to the right to claim damages held by victims, persons harmed, or their surviving family members who had already been notified of a truth-finding decision by the Commission as of the enforcement date of this Act; provided, a person who received a truth-finding decision before the enforcement of this Act (including a person whose statute of limitations has expired under Article 766(1) of the Civil Act and a person who has received a final judgment dismissing a claim with prejudice on the grounds of the expiration of the statute of limitations) may exercise the right to claim damages within 3 years from the date this Act enters into force (referring to the enforcement date of the Framework Act on Settling Past History for Truth and Reconciliation, Act No. 21330).
Article 6 (General transitional measures)
Any disposition, procedure or other acts under the previous provisions as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed taken pursuant to the corresponding provisions of this Act, if such provisions exist in this Act.
Article 7 (Transitional measures concerning truth-finding)
(1) For cases received by the former Commission under the previous provisions for which a decision was made to suspend the investigation on the grounds of the limitation of the investigation period, the Commission shall initiate a truth-finding investigation under the amended provisions of Article 25.
(2) Where an applicant requests a reinvestigation of a case received by the former Commission pursuant to the previous provisions in which the investigation had been insufficient, the Commission may decide to commence a truth-finding investigation pursuant to the amended provisions of Article 25 where it determines that additional truth-finding is necessary.
Article 8 (Transitional measures concerning succession and management of records)
(1) Records held by the former Commission under the previous provisions that fall under subparagraph 2 of Article 3 of the Public Records Management Act shall be succeeded to and managed by the Commission newly constituted under this Act.
(2) The Commission newly constituted under this Act shall be deemed the agency succeeding to the duties under Article 25(2) of the Public Records Management Act.
(3) An archives management institution under subparagraph 4 of Article 3 of the Public Records Management Act shall actively cooperate if the Commission newly constituted under this Act requests the provision of copies or perusal of records produced or collected by the former Commission.
Article 9 Omitted.
